title: RAIN
subtitle: Seventy-four Ashoka-cut diamonds. Fifty-two point twenty-four carats. Each stone suspended independently from a V-shaped chain, falling at its own length, catching light at its own angle. No two drops land the same way. That is not an accident — it is the entire idea. The Ashoka cut was chosen for a reason. Its geometry commands a room quietly — rectangular in proportion, architectural in its stillness, yet alive in a way step cuts rarely achieve. A single Ashoka on the hand draws attention. Seventy-four of them falling from the neck in graduated lengths do something else entirely. They move. In the right light, against the right skin, RAIN shifts with the body — a slow, continuous shimmer that follows every turn, every breath, every step.
